title: Marigold Retail - invoice embedding & gen cost optimization analysis
summary: Detailed before/after cost model for Marigold Retail's invoice-processing pipeline showing savings from Redwood Optimize recommendations (quantized reroute, prefix caching, batching, and embedding replacement for search). This sheet synthesizes raw telemetry + billing and proposes an implementable rollout with estimated savings and risk notes.
executive_summary: Marigold currently spends an estimated $46,200/mo on LLM inference for invoice ingestion, OCR normalization prompts, line-item extraction generations, and search/reranking. Redwood Optimize recommendations reduce estimated cost to $12,900/mo (≈72% savings) by: 1) replacing full-text generation for search with dense embeddings + kNN on cheaper CPU instances for most queries, 2) routing mid-latency requests to a 4-bit quantized Llama-3-7B-vq variant, 3) enabling prefix/KV caching for repetitive invoice templates, and 4) adjusting batching/timeout windows. Recommended rollout: staged A/B canary across 10/30/100% with quality gates tied to existing eval prompts.
assumptions: Baseline traffic: 18M tokens/month across generation routes; 3M embedding vectors/month; 25k inference requests/day; median request latency target = 500ms

Baseline models: lla-3-32b (gen) for extraction and reranking; emb-large-v2 for embedding; effective per-token hosted cost (Marigold contract) assumed $0.0045/token for gen models and $0.0008/embedding vector
Quantized variant token-cost assumption: 4x cheaper CPU/GPU unit economics vs baseline hosted 32B when served in Dedicated with Redwood Optimize (modeled as $0.0011/token equivalent)
Caching hit-rate: prefix/KV caching expected to reduce tokens served by 28% on templates after warm-up; sensitivity 15–40%
Batching improvements: average token latency margin allows increasing batch window to 25ms, improving throughput and reducing per-token cost by ~8% for gen routes
No changes to SLAs beyond allowable 10% tail-latency increase for non-critical routes; safety/PII handling unchanged
baseline_snapshot:
Baseline monthly cost breakdown (observed billing + telemetry):
- Generative extraction (lla-3-32b): $29,700/mo (12.5M tokens)
- Reranking/QA generations: $8,100/mo (3.6M tokens)
- Embeddings for search/indexing (emb-large-v2): $7,800/mo (3M vectors)
- Other infra/overhead: $1,600/mo
Total baseline: $47,200/mo (rounded to $46.2k in earlier communications due to billing windows)
Note: baseline includes a 7% buffer for retries and spikes. Token counts derived from logs July 2025.
recommended_changes: Replace full-text gen-based search/reranking with embeddings-powered approximate nearest neighbor (ANN) lookup for 72% of queries; keep gen-rerank for top 10% confidence-critical queries
Deploy 4-bit quantized Llama-3-7B-vq on Dedicated capacity for extract/generation workflows where latency < 700ms is acceptable
Enable per-customer prefix/KV caching for recurring invoice templates; warm-up via historical ingestion replay during rollout
Adjust batching window to 25–30ms for low-latency batchable requests and increase max_batch_size to reduce per-token overhead
Add a traffic policy: route by latency-cost policy (hot path to baseline gen, warm path to quantized model, cold path to cheap embed-only flow)
Add evaluation hooks: daily quality checks on a fixed prompt set (50 canonical invoices) with automatic rollback on >3% delta in extraction F1
before_after_table:
Before -> After (monthly):
- Generative extraction: $29,700 -> $9,200  (switch to 7B quantized + caching)
- Reranking: $8,100 -> $1,400  (embeddings for bulk + gen for top 10%)
- Embeddings: $7,800 -> $1,900  (migrate to CPU-hosted ANN + batching, lower per-vector cost)
- Infra/overhead: $1,600 -> $400  (reduced AI-hosted bandwidth and retries)
Total: $47,200 -> $12,900  (approx $34,300/mo savings, ~72% reduction)
estimated_savings_explanation: Savings drivers: quantized model reduces token compute cost by ~60-75% for generation-heavy routes; embedding migration of bulk reranking removes repeated generation calls; caching reduces repeat token emission by ~28%; batching and routing add another ~15% stack-level reduction. Conservative scenario (lower caching 15% and quantization benefits at 40%) yields ~$18k/mo savings (~38%). Aggressive scenario (high cache hit and full routing adoption) yields +80% savings. All scenarios included in sensitivity table tab.
sensitivity_notes: Cache hit-rate variance +/-10% changes monthly savings by +/- $4k
If 7B quantized quality causes rollback on >3% eval delta, fallback cost would be +$3.2k/mo while running dual paths during canary
Embedding per-vector cost sensitivity: +/- $0.0005/vector changes savings by up to $6k/mo
Traffic growth of 20% increases absolute savings but reduces percentage savings slightly if growth is concentrated on extraction requests
implementation_plan:
1) Week 0–2: synthetic replay + offline evals (run historical June–July invoice corpus through quantized 7B and emb-ANN to validate F1/ndcg).
2) Week 2–4: small canary (10% traffic) with feature flags and telemetry (latency, F1, cost per request).
3) Week 5–6: 30% ramp pending quality gates; enable KV caching for top 5 templates.
4) Week 6–8: 100% ramp with scheduling of dedicated instances and SLO changes; finalize cost allocation changes to billing dashboard.
5) Post-rollout: 6-week monitoring period and monthly check-in with Marigold engineering to tune models and cache TTLs.
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: quality regressions when using 7B quantized model for extraction — mitigation: dual-write (gen + quant) for first 2 weeks and automatic rollback if F1 drops >3%. Risk: embedding ANN recall drop affecting business metrics — mitigation: hybrid rerank: ANN candidate set + light gen-rerank for top-K. Risk: infra provisioning mismatch — mitigation: pre-provision Dedicated capacity window with temporary burst allowance.
